carbon_pricing.name: Kazakhstan Emissions Trading System (KAZ ETS)
carbon_pricing.price: US$1/tCO2e (KZT455), World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard, 2026

KAZ.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 9 Nov 2024; technical expert review report published as FCCC/ETF/TERR.1/2024/KAZ.

IRQ.notes: Iraq’s 2025 NDC 3.0 is more quantitative than its earlier NDC and is centered on oil-and-gas flaring reduction, power-sector transition, renewables, transport, industry, agriculture and waste, but Iraq has no compliance carbon tax or ETS in force as of 2026; official documents discuss carbon markets/Article 6 capacity-building rather than a domestic compliance price.
IRQ.ndc_target: Up to 5% unconditional GHG reduction below BAU by 2035, plus up to 17% conditional on international support (total up to 22% below BAU); also up to 3% unconditional below BAU by 2030.
IRQ.paris_status: Party; signed 8 Dec 2016, ratified 1 Nov 2021, in force for Iraq 1 Dec 2021.
IRQ.latest_un_report: BTR1 / 2024 Biennial Transparency Report, submitted/published by UNFCCC in 2025.

PAK.notes: Pakistan submitted NDC 3.0 on 24 Sep 2025; it has carbon-market guidelines and is developing voluntary/compliance market infrastructure, but the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard lists the Pakistan ETS as only “under consideration,” so no in-force ETS or carbon tax price is reported.
PAK.ndc_target: -50% GHG by 2035 vs business-as-usual/projection, comprising 17% unconditional and 33% conditional on international finance, technology transfer and capacity support.
PAK.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 10 Nov 2016.
PAK.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 31 Dec 2024; related CTF tables submitted 08 Jul 2025 and CRT submitted 06 Feb 2026.

UKR.notes: Ukraine has a carbon tax in force, while a national ETS is still under development rather than operating as a live priced market as of 2026; the 2025 NDC2 and 2026 LT-LEDS align policy toward 2050 climate neutrality amid war and reconstruction pressures.
UKR.ndc_target: Reduce GHG emissions in 2035 by more than 65% from 1990 levels.
UKR.paris_status: Party; ratified 19 September 2016, Paris Agreement in force for Ukraine from 4 November 2016.

carbon_pricing.name: Environmental tax on carbon dioxide emissions from stationary sources
carbon_pricing.price: UAH 30/tCO2, reported as of 2024 and reflected in the current Tax Code materials

carbon_pricing.name: National Emissions Trading System
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

UKR.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 29 Oct 2025; NID and CRT submitted 30 Dec 2024.

MYS.notes: Malaysia has announced plans for a national carbon tax for iron, steel and energy and a domestic ETS/carbon-market framework, but as of 25 Oct 2026 no national carbon tax or mandatory ETS with a published compliance price appears to be in force; Bursa Carbon Exchange is voluntary, not an ETS.
MYS.ndc_target: Peak GHG emissions between 2029 and 2034, strive to peak by 2030, and reduce 15–30 MtCO2e by 2035 below the peak level (up to 20 MtCO2e unconditional; 10 MtCO2e conditional).
MYS.paris_status: Party; ratified 16 November 2016, in force for Malaysia 16 December 2016.
MYS.latest_un_report: First Biennial Transparency Report (BTR1), submitted December 2024.

NGA.notes: Nigeria’s Climate Change Act 2021 legally requires carbon budgets and mechanisms for carbon tax and emissions trading and sets a net-zero window of 2050–2070, while the specific 2060 net-zero year is set out in Nigeria’s LT-LEDS/Energy Transition Plan; no national ETS is in force as of 2026.
NGA.ndc_target: Economy-wide absolute emissions reduction of 184.9 MtCO₂e in 2035 vs 2018 emissions of 573.5 MtCO₂e, equivalent to a 32.2% reduction.
NGA.paris_status: Party; ratified 16 May 2017 and entered into force for Nigeria 15 June 2017.

carbon_pricing.name: Nigeria gas flaring tax
carbon_pricing.price: US$7/tCO₂e-equivalent, 2026 World Bank dashboard; applies to unauthorized flaring/venting and is not a general carbon tax.

TWN.notes: Taiwan’s 2050 net-zero goal was written into the Climate Change Response Act promulgated on Feb. 15, 2023; an ETS/cap-and-trade system is planned or in trial design, but no mandatory ETS is in force as of 2026.
TWN.ndc_target: -38% ±2% net GHG emissions by 2035 vs 2005; interim 2030 target -28% ±2% vs 2005
TWN.paris_status: none — Taiwan is not a UNFCCC/Paris Agreement Party and cannot sign or ratify, but says it voluntarily aligns with Paris/UNFCCC norms

carbon_pricing.name: Carbon fee under the Climate Change Response Act
carbon_pricing.price: NT$300/tCO2e standard rate in force from 2025; preferential rates NT$50 or NT$100/tCO2e for approved self-determined reduction plans

TWN.latest_un_report: none — no official UNFCCC transparency report submission; Taiwan published a voluntary first Biennial Transparency Report in Nov 2025

BGD.notes: Bangladesh’s latest NDC is its 2025 NDC 3.0; it frames mitigation around a BAU-relative 2035 target and refers to moving toward a net-zero path around 2050, but no carbon tax or ETS is in force.
BGD.ndc_target: 2035 economy-wide GHG reduction vs BAU: 6.39% unconditional; 13.92% conditional on international support.
BGD.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 21 Sep 2016, in force 4 Nov 2016.

carbon_pricing.name: none
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

VEN.notes: Venezuela’s second NDC for 2025–2030 was recorded by the UNFCCC on 28 Oct 2025 and says the country aims to maintain carbon neutrality, but it does not set a dated net-zero year; the World Bank carbon-pricing dashboard lists no implemented Venezuelan ETS or carbon tax, so carbon pricing is recorded as none.
VEN.ndc_target: Reduce GHG emissions by 20% by 2030 relative to a baseline/business-as-usual scenario.
VEN.paris_status: Party; ratified 21 Jul 2017, in force for Venezuela 20 Aug 2017.
VEN.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 02 Jan 2025; UNFCCC publication date 19 Feb 2025.

NLD.notes: The Netherlands participates in the EU’s joint NDC, while national law and policy set Dutch targets of climate neutrality by 2050 and a 55% emissions cut by 2030; UNFCCC reporting for the Netherlands covers the European part of the Kingdom.
NLD.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: reduce net GHG emissions by 66.25%–72.5% by 2035 vs 1990; Netherlands’ domestic Climate Act target remains -55% by 2030 vs 1990.
NLD.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 28 Jul 2017

COL.notes: Colombia’s 2026 profile combines a legally anchored 2050 carbon-neutrality goal and carbon tax with a newly regulated ETS framework whose compliance market price is not yet observable.
COL.ndc_target: Cap national GHG emissions at 155–161 MtCO2e by 2035; 2030 goal retained to cut GHG emissions 51% vs BAU / limit emissions to 169.4 MtCO2e.

carbon_pricing.name: Impuesto Nacional al Carbono
carbon_pricing.price: COP 29,070.49/tCO2e in 2026; coal at 50% of full rate in 2026

carbon_pricing.name: Programa Nacional de Cupos Transables de Emisión de GEI (PNCTE)
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

ESP.notes: Spain is covered by the EU’s joint NDC and EU ETS, while its domestic climate law (Law 7/2021) anchors the 2050 climate-neutrality objective; the 2026 national policy debate is mainly about implementing EU-wide targets through Spain’s NECP and sectoral measures.
ESP.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: at least -55% net GHG by 2030 vs 1990, plus an indicative 2035 contribution of -66.25% to -72.5% vs 1990 in the latest 2025 EU NDC.
ESP.paris_status: Party; Spain ratified the Paris Agreement on 12 Jan 2017.

carbon_pricing.name: EU ETS 1 (stationary installations, aviation, maritime; applies in Spain)
carbon_pricing.price: EUR 78.93/tCO2e average allowance price, Apr-Sep 2026 (European Commission Article 29a indicator)

carbon_pricing.name: Spanish tax on fluorinated greenhouse gases
carbon_pricing.price: EUR 15/tCO2e formula rate (0.015 × GWP per kg; cap EUR 100/kg), 2026

carbon_pricing.price: EUR 0.15/GJ for professional uses except power/cogeneration; EUR 0.65/GJ for other uses, 2026

ESP.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 7 Nov 2024; latest UNFCCC reporting entries also show 2026 NID/CRT inventory submissions on 14 Apr 2026.

QAT.notes: Qatar’s NDC 3.0, submitted 21 Nov 2025, replaces its earlier 2030 BAU-relative pledge; no official economy-wide net-zero target or in-force national carbon tax/ETS was found in official UNFCCC/Qatari sources or the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard as of 2026.
QAT.ndc_target: Mitigation actions equivalent to 42 MtCO2e of GHG emission reductions by 2040, moving away from a BAU-relative target.
QAT.paris_status: Party; ratified Paris Agreement on 23 Jun 2017.

PHL.notes: The Philippines’ 2026 NDC was submitted on 8 Sep 2026 and says current modelling could make the country a net sink over 2025–2035, but the country still has no adopted net-zero target and no carbon tax or mandatory ETS in force; a national carbon-market framework was ordered in Oct 2026 but is not yet an in-force ETS or tax.
PHL.ndc_target: 75% net GHG emissions reduction and/or avoidance, including FOLU, over 2025–2035 vs projected BAU cumulative emissions; 7% unconditional and 68% conditional on international support
PHL.paris_status: Party; ratified 23 Mar 2017, entry into force for the Philippines 22 Apr 2017
PHL.latest_un_report: BTR1 / 2024 Biennial Transparency Report, submitted 31 Mar 2025

TKM.notes: Turkmenistan’s current NDC is active in the UNFCCC registry and economy-wide in framing, while no national carbon tax or ETS is listed as implemented in the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard and no official net-zero target was found in UNFCCC/government climate submissions reviewed.
TKM.ndc_target: 20% GHG reduction by 2030 compared with a business-as-usual scenario relative to 2010 emission levels
TKM.paris_status: Party; signed 23 Sep 2016 and ratified 20 Oct 2016

UZB.notes: Uzbekistan’s latest NDC is intensity-based rather than an absolute emissions cap; its NDC 3.0 also says the country is discussing a Low-Carbon Development Strategy to 2055 and aims for net-zero emissions by 2055–2060, but no binding net-zero law was found. A 2025 greenhouse-gas-emissions law creates MRV, registry and carbon-unit trading architecture, but official/World Bank sources describe carbon pricing as potential/under development, not an ETS or carbon tax with compliance obligations and a market price in force.
UZB.ndc_target: Reduce specific GHG emissions (emissions intensity) per unit of GDP by 50% by 2035 vs 2010 levels.
UZB.paris_status: Party; signed 19 Apr 2017 and ratified in 2018 under Law No. LRU-491.
UZB.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 29 Dec 2024; CTF-NDC resubmitted 18 Apr 2025; technical expert review report published 22 Sep 2026.

ETH.notes: Ethiopia’s current NDC 3.0 was submitted to the UNFCCC on 26 Sep 2025; the government also has a 2025 Carbon Market Strategy and Article 6 interest, but no domestic carbon tax or ETS in force was listed in the World Bank carbon-pricing dashboard.
ETH.ndc_target: 70.3% GHG reduction by 2035 below revised business-as-usual, including 40.7% unconditional and the remainder conditional on international support.
ETH.paris_status: Party; ratified 9 Mar 2017, in force for Ethiopia 8 Apr 2017.
ETH.latest_un_report: BUR1, 11 Jun 2024; UNFCCC BTR1 table showed no Ethiopia BTR submission as of its 8 Sep 2026 update.

OMN.notes: Oman has moved from its 2023 updated 2030 NDC to a 2026 NDC 3.0 with a 2035 target, while its carbon-market work is framed around Article 6/crediting rather than an in-force carbon tax or ETS.
OMN.ndc_target: Unconditional 7% and conditional 26% GHG reduction by 2035 against a 2024 baseline under Oman NDC 3.0.
OMN.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified in 2019.
OMN.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 26 Oct 2025; CTF-NDC and CRT submitted 28 Oct 2025.

BEL.notes: Belgium’s headline NDC is the joint EU NDC rather than a standalone national NDC; Belgium has no fuel-based carbon tax or direct GHG-emissions tax, and its main explicit carbon price is the EU ETS.
BEL.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: at least -55% net domestic GHG emissions by 2030 vs 1990, no international credits
BEL.paris_status: Party; Belgium ratified the Paris Agreement on 6 Apr 2017

CHL.notes: Chile has no economy-wide GHG ETS in force; its carbon-pricing framework is centered on the green tax plus an emissions-offsetting system for liable taxpayers, while the 2025 NDC continues the legally anchored 2050 carbon-neutrality pathway.
CHL.ndc_target: GHG emissions cap of 90 MtCO2e in 2035, within a 2021-2035/2020-2035 carbon-budget framework and peaking in 2025.
CHL.paris_status: Party; Chile ratified the Paris Agreement on 10 Feb 2017.

carbon_pricing.name: Impuesto Verde / CO2 tax on large stationary sources

LBY.notes: Libya launched/endorsed its first NDC, NAP and Initial National Communication domestically on 7 July 2026, but its own NDC says Libya only signed the Paris Agreement in 2016 and intends to ratify it; therefore Paris/BTR obligations and registry status should be treated cautiously until UN depositary/UNFCCC records change.
LBY.ndc_target: Reduce carbon intensity 28% by 2035 vs 2023 using domestic resources, or 49% conditional on international support.
LBY.latest_un_report: none; UNFCCC non-Annex I national communication table shows no Libya NC, and no BTR/BUR was found as of Oct 2026.

ROU.notes: Romania has no separate national NDC outside the EU joint NDC; its 2050 neutrality goal is set through the government-approved long-term strategy “România Neutră în 2050,” while European Parliament analysis notes Romania still lacks a dedicated climate framework law.
ROU.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: net GHG reduction of 66.25–72.5% by 2035 vs 1990; it also reiterates at least -55% net GHG by 2030 vs 1990.
ROU.paris_status: Party; Romania ratified the Paris Agreement on 1 June 2017 and it entered into force for Romania on 1 July 2017.

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS / ETS1), applying in Romania as an EU member state
carbon_pricing.price: €78.93/tCO2e average EUA price for Apr–Sep 2026; recent EEX common-platform clearing prices were about €84–86/tCO2e in late Sep/early Oct 2026.

ROU.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 30 Jan 2026 to the UNFCCC.

KWT.notes: Kuwait is a Non-Annex I, oil-export-dependent Party; its official 2060 low-carbon roadmap and KPC materials frame the national net-zero objective as 2050 for oil and gas operations and 2060 for other sectors, while no carbon tax or ETS is listed as implemented in the World Bank carbon-pricing dashboard.
KWT.ndc_target: Reduce economy-wide GHG emissions 7.4% below business-as-usual by 2035.
KWT.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 23 Apr 2018, in force 23 May 2018.
KWT.latest_un_report: No BTR submitted as of Oct 2026; latest transparency report is BUR1, submitted 30 Sep 2019.

BLR.notes: Belarus submitted its 2026–2035 NDC to the UNFCCC on 10 Nov 2025; the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard/State and Trends materials do not list an implemented Belarus carbon tax or ETS, so no direct carbon-pricing instrument is recorded here.
BLR.ndc_target: Unconditional economy-wide GHG reduction of at least 42% by 2035 vs 1990; conditional target up to 47% with international support.
BLR.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 21 Sep 2016.

PER.notes: Peru’s latest NDC 3.0 was published by the UNFCCC on 6 Nov 2025; the 2050 net-zero goal is set in the National Climate Change Strategy to 2050 approved by Supreme Decree, while OECD/World Bank carbon-pricing sources indicate no explicit carbon tax or ETS is in force as of 2026.
PER.ndc_target: Limit net GHG emissions to 179 MtCO2e in 2035, conditional on international climate finance, technical cooperation and technology transfer.
PER.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 25 Jul 2016.
PER.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 31 Dec 2024; UNFCCC page lists BTR publication/update on 7 Jan 2025 and CRT on 30 Sep 2025.

CZE.notes: Czechia’s Paris targets are submitted jointly through the EU; it has no separate national NDC headline target, and its binding net-zero obligation is the EU-wide 2050 climate-neutrality target under the European Climate Law rather than a standalone Czech climate law.
CZE.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: net GHG reduction of 66.25%–72.5% by 2035 vs 1990, while reiterating at least -55% by 2030 vs 1990
CZE.paris_status: Party; ratified 5 Oct 2017, entered into force for Czech Republic 4 Nov 2017

TZA.notes: Tanzania has carbon-trading regulations for voluntary/Article 6 carbon-credit projects, but these are not a domestic carbon tax or compliance ETS with an official allowance/tax price; its 2050 net-zero reference appears in a May 2025 draft Long-Term Vision, not in law or a UNFCCC-submitted LT-LEDS.
TZA.ndc_target: Reduce economy-wide GHG emissions by 30–35% below business-as-usual by 2030, equivalent to about 138–153 MtCO2e gross reductions.
TZA.paris_status: Party; ratified 18 May 2018, in force for Tanzania 17 June 2018.
TZA.latest_un_report: none (no BTR1 or BUR submitted in UNFCCC submission tables as of 2026).

SGP.notes: Singapore has no domestic ETS in force; its carbon-pricing instrument is a broad carbon tax covering about 70% of national emissions, while its latest NDC is a 2035 absolute emissions limit and builds on the 2030 target of around 60 MtCO2e.
SGP.ndc_target: Reduce economy-wide GHG emissions to 45–50 MtCO2e in 2035.
SGP.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 21 Sep 2016.

NOR.notes: Norway’s legally anchored long-term Climate Change Act target is a low-emission society by 2050, with a 90–95% emissions-reduction target by 2050, while the 2030 climate-neutrality objective relies on cooperation/credits rather than being the headline NDC target.
NOR.ndc_target: Reduce GHG emissions by at least 70–75% by 2035 vs 1990 levels, economy-wide.

TCD.notes: Chad’s active NDC 3.0 was submitted to the UNFCCC on 5 Oct 2026 and prioritizes adaptation alongside a modest mitigation target; the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard lists implemented carbon-pricing instruments globally, but none for Chad.

PRK.notes: DPR Korea’s current UNFCCC-listed NDC is its First NDC updated submission dated 19 Sep 2019; official UNFCCC report listings show no separate long-term net-zero strategy, BTR or BUR submission, and major carbon-pricing trackers list no implemented DPRK ETS or carbon tax.
PRK.ndc_target: Reduce GHG emissions 16.4% below BAU by 2030 unconditionally, and up to 52% below BAU by 2030 with international support.
PRK.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 1 Aug 2016, entry into force 4 Nov 2016.
PRK.latest_un_report: none; UNFCCC records list no BTR/BUR for DPR Korea as of 2026, only NC1, NC2 and NDC submissions.

SDN.notes: Sudan is an LDC and its current UNFCCC-registered NDC is sectoral rather than economy-wide, focused on energy, forestry/biomass and waste; no compliance carbon tax or ETS is listed as implemented by the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard.
SDN.ndc_target: By 2030 vs BAU: energy (non-biomass) -38%, forestry & energy (biomass) -45%, waste -20%; total reductions about 27.1 MtCO2e, conditional on international support.
SDN.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 2 Aug 2017.
SDN.latest_un_report: BUR1, submitted 13 Apr 2025; no BTR listed for Sudan as of the UNFCCC 2026 BTR tables checked.

KEN.notes: Kenya’s 2023 Climate Change Act amendments and 2024/2026 carbon-market rules regulate voluntary and Article 6 carbon markets, but they do not constitute an in-force domestic carbon tax or ETS with a compliance price.
KEN.ndc_target: Reduce GHG emissions 35% by 2035 relative to a BAU scenario of 215 MtCO2e, abating 75.25 MtCO2e; partly conditional on international support.
KEN.paris_status: Party; Paris Agreement ratified on 28 Dec 2016.
KEN.latest_un_report: BTR1 / First Biennial Transparency Report, submitted Dec 2024.

MAR.notes: Morocco’s 2025 NDC 3.0 frames policy around a low-carbon development pathway to 2050 and Article 6 carbon-market cooperation, but the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard lists Morocco’s carbon tax only as under consideration, not in force, and no implemented ETS.
MAR.ndc_target: -53% GHG by 2035 vs BAU, comprising 21.6% unconditional and 31.4% conditional reductions

MNG.notes: Mongolia adopted its first dedicated Climate Change Law in July 2026, creating frameworks for MRV, climate finance and carbon-market mechanisms, but no domestic carbon tax or compliance ETS is in force as of 2026.
MNG.ndc_target: Unconditional 30.3% GHG reduction by 2035 versus baseline; 46.3% net incl. forest sink; conditional 52.8% net incl. sink and international support.
MNG.paris_status: Party; ratified 21 Sept 2016, in force 4 Nov 2016.
MNG.latest_un_report: BTR1 / 2024 Biennial Transparency Report, submitted 30 Dec 2025.

MMR.notes: Myanmar’s net-zero reference is limited to forestry and other land use (FOLU)—an aspirational conditional target in its updated first NDC—not an economy-wide net-zero law; the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard lists no implemented Myanmar ETS or carbon tax.
MMR.ndc_target: 2030 sectoral NDC: 244.5 MtCO2e unconditional and 414.8 MtCO2e conditional cumulative emissions avoided/reduced in 2021–2030, mainly energy and FOLU, not economy-wide.
MMR.paris_status: Party; ratified 19 Sep 2017, in force for Myanmar 19 Oct 2017.
MMR.latest_un_report: none (no BTR1 or BUR listed by UNFCCC as of Sep 2026; latest UNFCCC national report listed is NC1, submitted/published 2012).

NZL.notes: New Zealand has a split-gas domestic 2050 target in the Climate Change Response Act: net zero for all GHGs other than biogenic methane, plus separate biogenic methane reductions; its 2021–2030 NDC1 remains 50% below gross 2005 levels by 2030 while NDC2 covers 2031–2035.
NZL.ndc_target: Reduce net greenhouse gas emissions 51–55% below gross 2005 levels by 2035
NZL.paris_status: Party; ratified 4 Oct 2016, in force for New Zealand 4 Nov 2016

HKG.notes: Hong Kong’s own policy target is to reduce carbon emissions by 50% before 2035 compared with 2005 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2050; as of 2026 it has no carbon tax or mandatory ETS in force.
HKG.ndc_target: No separate Hong Kong NDC; Hong Kong is covered by China’s Paris Agreement NDC. Current China 2035 NDC headline: reduce economy-wide net GHG emissions by 7–10% from peak levels by 2035, striving to do better.
HKG.paris_status: Party via China; China ratified the Paris Agreement on 3 Sep 2016 and announced its application to the Hong Kong SAR.
HKG.latest_un_report: China BTR1, submitted 31 Dec 2024; includes Hong Kong SAR information.

ISR.notes: Israel’s 2050 net-zero goal has been announced politically, while the climate bill that would enshrine net zero and a stronger 2030 target had not completed enactment in the sources checked; Israel has no ETS in force.
ISR.ndc_target: Unconditional economy-wide net GHG reduction of 27% by 2030 vs 2015, capping emissions at 58 MtCO2e.
ISR.paris_status: Party; ratified 22 Nov 2016, entered into force for Israel 22 Dec 2016.

ISR.latest_un_report: BTR1 / NC4 submitted 3 Apr 2025; NID 5 May 2025; CRT 31 Aug 2025.

PRT.notes: Portugal is covered by the EU’s joint NDC and EU ETS; nationally, the Climate Framework Law sets binding domestic GHG-reduction milestones against 2005 levels, while the 2045 carbon-neutrality objective is stated in the revised NECP/government policy rather than yet fully reflected as a distinct statutory net-zero year.

carbon_pricing.name: Portugal carbon charge on air and sea travel
carbon_pricing.price: €2 per ticket (World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard, 2025/2026 factsheet)

AZE.notes: Azerbaijan’s current NDC 3.0, submitted in November 2025, strengthened the previous 2023 NDC headline from a conditional 40% cut by 2050 to a conditional 40% cut by 2035, but it still does not set an economy-wide net-zero target or an implemented domestic carbon tax/ETS.
AZE.ndc_target: -40% GHG emissions by 2035 vs 1990, conditional on finance, technology transfer/availability, capacity-building and absorptive capacity of forests/ecosystems
AZE.paris_status: Party; ratified 9 Jan 2017, in force for Azerbaijan 8 Feb 2017
AZE.latest_un_report: BTR1 submitted 21 Nov 2024; CRT submitted 31 Dec 2024

AUT.notes: Austria’s 2040 climate-neutrality goal is a national policy target, but as of 25 Oct 2026 the federal Climate Act intended to embed climate-neutrality governance was still a draft under consultation, not enacted; Austria also has a binding EU Effort Sharing Regulation target of -48% by 2030 vs 2005 for ESR sectors.
AUT.ndc_target: EU/Austria NDC: reduce net greenhouse-gas emissions by 66.25%–72.5% by 2035 vs 1990; existing 2030 EU target remains at least -55% net vs 1990.
AUT.paris_status: Party; Austria ratified on 5 Oct 2016 and the Paris Agreement entered into force for Austria on 4 Nov 2016.

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS I) in Austria
carbon_pricing.price: EUR 78.93/tCO2e average allowance price, Apr–Sep 2026; EUR 82.32/tCO2e Q3 2026 average used for CBAM certificates

carbon_pricing.name: Austria National Emissions Certificate Trading System (NEHG 2022)
carbon_pricing.price: EUR 55/tCO2 in 2026 for national emissions certificates

carbon_pricing.name: Standalone national carbon tax
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

AUT.latest_un_report: BTR1, Dec 2024; Austria’s 2026 NID says the first NIR/NID under the Paris Agreement was submitted in Dec 2024 together with Austria’s first Biennial Transparency Report.

GRC.notes: Greece is covered by the joint EU NDC; Greece’s National Climate Law 4936/2022 sets climate neutrality by 2050 plus domestic interim targets of at least -55% net GHG by 2030 and -80% by 2040 vs 1990; no explicit national carbon tax is listed here because Greece’s main explicit carbon-pricing instrument is the EU ETS.
GRC.ndc_target: Indicative net GHG reduction of 66.25%–72.5% by 2035 vs 1990; the EU/Greece 2030 NDC target of at least -55% net GHG vs 1990 remains active.

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS/ETS1)
carbon_pricing.price: EUR 78.93/tCO2e average allowance price, Apr–Sep 2026

carbon_pricing.name: Carbon taxes
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

ECU.notes: Ecuador has a long-term mitigation roadmap, PLANMICC 2024-2070, aimed at low-emissions development to 2070, but official sources reviewed do not state an economy-wide net-zero target; Ecuador has voluntary/Article 6 carbon-market frameworks under development, but no compliance carbon tax or ETS in force as of 2026.
ECU.ndc_target: Unconditional 7% GHG reduction by 2035 vs BAU/2010 baseline (about 8.8 MtCO2e); conditional additional 8% with international support (about 10.6 MtCO2e), i.e. up to 15% total.
ECU.paris_status: Party; ratified 20 September 2017, entry into force for Ecuador 20 October 2017.
ECU.latest_un_report: BTR1 / Fifth National Communication, submitted 27 Dec 2024; NID, CRT and CTF tables also submitted 27 Dec 2024.

AGO.notes: Angola’s active NDC 3.0 was submitted on 13 Sep 2025; the NDC mentions a commitment to global carbon neutrality but does not set an Angola-specific net-zero year, and World Bank carbon-pricing data show no implemented Angola carbon tax or ETS.
AGO.ndc_target: Unconditional 5% GHG reduction by 2035 vs 2020 BAU; conditional increase to 11% with international financial, technical and technological support.
AGO.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 16 Nov 2020, in force for Angola 16 Dec 2020.
AGO.latest_un_report: BUR1, submitted 24 Dec 2024; Angola had no BTR listed in the UNFCCC reports registry as of Oct 2026.

IRL.notes: Ireland does not submit a standalone national NDC target; it is covered by the EU and its Member States’ joint NDC, while national law also sets Ireland’s domestic 2050 climate-neutrality objective and carbon-budget framework.
IRL.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: indicative 66.25–72.5% net GHG reduction by 2035 vs 1990; reiterates at least -55% by 2030 vs 1990.

carbon_pricing.name: Ireland carbon tax (MOTCC/NGCT/SFCT)
carbon_pricing.price: €71/tCO2 standard Budget 2026 rate; some current fuel rates remain €63.50/tCO2 or €48.50/tCO2 depending on fuel/use

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)
carbon_pricing.price: €78.93/tCO2 average allowance price, Apr–Sep 2026, reported by European Commission for Oct 2026 Article 29a monitoring

IRL.latest_un_report: BTR1, 23 Dec 2024; NID and CRT submitted 18 Dec 2024

SWE.notes: Sweden reports under the joint EU NDC but has a stronger national 2045 net-zero framework; the Climate Act requires annual climate reporting and a climate policy action plan every four years.
SWE.ndc_target: EU/Sweden NDC: at least -55% net GHG by 2030 vs 1990, plus an indicative -66.25% to -72.5% net GHG contribution by 2035 vs 1990.

carbon_pricing.name: Swedish carbon tax
carbon_pricing.price: SEK 1,520/tCO2 for natural gas and coal in 2026 (about EUR 138/tCO2)

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)
carbon_pricing.price: EUR 78.93/tCO2e average EUA price for Apr-Sep 2026; EC-published CBAM/EU ETS reference price EUR 82.32/tCO2e for Q3 2026

SWE.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 19 Dec 2024; NID/CRT resubmitted 15 Apr 2025; technical expert review report issued 30 Jul 2025 and reissued 7 Aug 2025

FIN.notes: Finland’s 2035 carbon-neutrality goal is among the earliest legally enshrined national net-zero targets in the EU, but official 2026 reporting says additional measures are still needed, especially for land use sinks.
FIN.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: net GHG emissions reduction of 66.25–72.5% by 2035 vs 1990; Finland has no separate national NDC.

carbon_pricing.name: Finland carbon tax on fossil fuels / energy excise CO2 component
carbon_pricing.price: Product-specific in 2026; examples from Finnish Tax Administration: coal CO2 tax €147.81/t and natural gas CO2 tax €12.94/MWh for 1 Apr–31 Dec 2026; World Bank main rate: €51/tCO2e in 2026.

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS1)
carbon_pricing.price: EUA about €86/tCO2e on 23–25 Oct 2026.

FIN.latest_un_report: First Biennial Transparency Report (BTR1), submitted 19 Dec 2024.

HUN.notes: Hungary is covered by the EU’s joint NDC, while its domestic 2024 NECP states a national 2030 GHG-reduction commitment of at least 50% vs 1990; the 2050 climate-neutrality goal is in Hungary’s 2020 Climate Protection Act.
HUN.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: net GHG emissions reduction of 66.25%–72.5% by 2035 vs 1990; 2030 target of at least -55% net GHG vs 1990 reiterated.

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)
carbon_pricing.price: US$85 (€73)/tCO2e, 2026 (World Bank price as of Apr. 1, 2026)

SYR.notes: Syria’s current UNFCCC NDC is its first NDC, dated November 2018 and available in the UNFCCC NDC registry; it is framed around post-war reconstruction constraints and international support rather than a quantified emissions cap or reduction percentage.
SYR.ndc_target: No quantified economy-wide GHG-reduction target; qualitative voluntary mitigation/adaptation policies for 2020–2030, including sector measures such as a 10% renewable-energy target by 2030.
SYR.latest_un_report: No BTR or BUR submitted as of UNFCCC tables updated in 2026; latest UNFCCC national climate report found is Initial National Communication, 2010.

COD.notes: DRC’s mitigation profile is dominated by forests and land use; its 2023 legal changes and 2026 carbon-market ordinance point to carbon-market governance, but the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard does not list an implemented DRC ETS or priced tax instrument with a published rate.
COD.ndc_target: Unconditional 2% and conditional 21% GHG-emissions reduction by 2030 versus business-as-usual, with the conditional share dependent on international support.
COD.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 13 Dec 2017, in force for DRC 12 Jan 2018.

carbon_pricing.name: Carbon tax / carbon-pricing provisions under 2023 environment-law amendment
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

COD.latest_un_report: First Biennial Update Report (BUR1), submitted 30 Dec 2022; no BTR submission found in UNFCCC listings as of Oct 2026.

BOL.notes: Bolivia’s current NDC is strongly sectoral and highly conditional: it says the average conditionality of its targets is 74%, dependent on international climate finance, technology transfer and capacity-building; the World Bank lists a Bolivia ETS only as under consideration, so no carbon tax or ETS is in force.
BOL.ndc_target: NDC 3.0 (2026–2035) has no single economy-wide GHG % target; it sets 36 sectoral targets, including cutting deforestation outside protected areas 80%, eliminating deforestation in protected areas, reaching 75% renewable electricity in the grid, and several quantified land/agriculture/waste/water targets by 2035.
BOL.paris_status: Party; ratified 5 Oct 2016, in force 4 Nov 2016.

SRB.notes: Serbia’s 2025 NDC 3.0 raises the target from the 2022 NDC’s 33.3% by 2030; Serbia has introduced a low fixed carbon tax as a CBAM-alignment step but has no domestic ETS in force and no adopted net-zero/climate-neutrality target.
SRB.ndc_target: Conditional economy-wide GHG reduction of 40.1% by 2035 vs 1990, excluding LULUCF.
SRB.paris_status: Party; ratified 25 July 2017, in force for Serbia 24 August 2017.

carbon_pricing.name: Serbia greenhouse gas emissions tax
carbon_pricing.price: EUR 4/tCO2e from 2026 (about US$5/tCO2e in World Bank dashboard)

carbon_pricing.name: Emissions trading system
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

SRB.latest_un_report: BTR1 / 2024 Biennial Transparency Report; original submission 31 Dec 2024, updated/submitted 16 Jan 2025; NID and CRT submitted 27 Dec 2024.

BGR.notes: Bulgaria has no separate national NDC outside the EU joint NDC; its own long-term strategy describes pathways toward climate neutrality, while the legally binding 2050 climate-neutrality objective is set at EU level under the European Climate Law.
BGR.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: at least -55% net GHG by 2030 vs 1990, plus indicative -66.25% to -72.5% by 2035 vs 1990

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) in Bulgaria
carbon_pricing.price: €78.93/tCO2e average allowance price for Apr–Sep 2026; recent common-platform auction clearing price €84.70/EUA on 1 Oct 2026

carbon_pricing.name: National carbon tax
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

BGR.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 2 Jan 2025; NID/CRT submitted 18 Dec 2024

DNK.notes: Denmark has a national Climate Act target of -70% GHG by 2030 vs 1990 and climate neutrality by 2050; the government has politically proposed/used a 2045 climate-neutrality aim and 110% reduction by 2050, but the legal Climate Act target remains 2050 as of the cited sources.
DNK.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: indicative economy-wide net GHG reduction of 66.25–72.5% by 2035 vs 1990; current 2030 NDC of at least 55% net reduction remains active.

carbon_pricing.name: Denmark carbon tax / CO2-afgift
carbon_pricing.price: DKK 750/tCO2e (about US$116) main rate in 2026; separate green-tax-reform path reaches DKK 750/tCO2 for non-ETS firms and DKK 375/tCO2 for ETS firms by 2030.

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)
carbon_pricing.price: EUR 78.93/tCO2 average allowance price for Apr–Sep 2026; World Bank dashboard lists about EUR 73/tCO2e (US$85) for 2026.

TUN.notes: Tunisia’s headline NDC is intensity-based rather than an absolute emissions cap; I found no implemented direct carbon tax or ETS with a CO2 price in the World Bank carbon-pricing dataset, despite references to preparatory carbon-pricing work and environmental/fuel-related taxes.
TUN.ndc_target: Reduce carbon intensity of the economy by 62% by 2035 vs 2010, with an interim 46.4% reduction by 2030.
TUN.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 10 Feb 2017, entered into force for Tunisia 12 Mar 2017.
TUN.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 30 Dec 2024; NID resubmitted/updated 25 Feb 2026.

BHR.notes: Bahrain’s NDC is framed as adaptation actions and economic-diversification measures with mitigation co-benefits; the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard lists a Bahrain carbon tax as under consideration, not implemented, so there is no carbon tax or ETS in force with a price.
BHR.ndc_target: NDC 3.0: by 2035, renewable-energy installed capacity equal to 20%, plus 1.8 million additional trees and 1.6 million mangrove seedlings; no economy-wide GHG reduction target.
BHR.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 23 Dec 2016.
BHR.latest_un_report: BTR1 (2024), submitted 30 Nov 2025; publication date 02 Dec 2025.

UGA.notes: Uganda has no economy-wide net-zero target or compliance carbon tax/ETS in force; its 2023 Energy Transition Plan instead sets an energy-sector net-zero target for 2065, and 2025 climate-change mechanism regulations govern carbon-credit markets rather than a mandatory ETS or carbon tax.
UGA.ndc_target: 24.7% economy-wide GHG reduction by 2030 below business-as-usual, with unconditional and conditional components
UGA.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 21 Sep 2016
UGA.latest_un_report: BUR2, 12 Aug 2025; no BTR1 listed on UNFCCC first-BTR submissions page as updated 8 Sep 2026

NPL.notes: Nepal’s 2045 net-zero CO2 goal is set out in its 2021 Long-term Strategy and referenced in NDC 3.0, while its 2025 Carbon Trading Regulation and national carbon registry relate to carbon markets/crediting rather than an in-force domestic carbon tax or ETS.
NPL.ndc_target: Reduce net GHG emissions by 17.12% in 2030 and 26.79% in 2035 below the business-as-usual scenario, with the majority conditional on international support.
NPL.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 5 Oct 2016.
NPL.latest_un_report: BTR1 / 2024 Biennial Transparency Report, submitted 9 Jun 2025.

GHA.notes: Ghana has no carbon tax or ETS in force as of 2026; it is instead operationalising Article 6 carbon-crediting/ITMO systems, and official reporting also notes a separate energy-transition plan pathway for net-zero energy-related carbon emissions by 2060.
GHA.ndc_target: Reduce 2030 GHG emissions by 64 MtCO2e: 24.6 MtCO2e unconditional and 39.4 MtCO2e conditional, covering CO2, CH4, N2O and HFCs across about 88% of emissions.
GHA.paris_status: Party; Ghana ratified the Paris Agreement on 21 September 2016 and it entered into force for Ghana on 4 November 2016.

CUB.notes: Cuba’s current NDC is not framed as an economy-wide absolute GHG-reduction target or net-zero pathway; as of 2026 it has a carbon-market/Article 6 regulatory framework, but no compliance carbon tax or ETS in force with an observable carbon price.
CUB.ndc_target: NDC 3.0 for 2031–2035: sectoral actions, headed by 26% renewable electricity generation by 2035, 15% electric vehicles in the national fleet, forestry expansion/management targets, and methane/emissions reductions in dairy and sugar-industry waste streams.
CUB.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 28 Dec 2016.
CUB.latest_un_report: BTR1 submitted 31 Mar 2025; 2024 CRT submitted 14 Apr 2025; REDD+ technical annex to BTR1 submitted 13 Apr 2026.

ZMB.notes: Zambia’s NDC 3.0 was submitted to the UNFCCC on 15 Dec 2025; it keeps the 2030 headline mitigation percentages but broadens sector coverage toward an economy-wide approach, while Zambia has carbon-market regulations for Article 6 but no domestic carbon tax or GHG ETS in force with a price.
ZMB.ndc_target: 25% unconditional (20,000 Gg CO2e) and 47% conditional (38,000 Gg CO2e) GHG reduction by 2030 vs BAU, base year 2010

CMR.notes: Cameroon’s 2026 NDC 3.0 raises ambition from its 2021 NDC and covers the whole national territory and CO2, CH4, N2O, HFCs, PFCs and SF6; carbon pricing is at feasibility/design discussion stage, not an in-force ETS or carbon tax.
CMR.ndc_target: -41% GHG by 2035 vs BAU2035, with -14% unconditional and -27% conditional; interim 2030 target is -38% (-13% unconditional, -25% conditional).
CMR.latest_un_report: No BTR1 listed; latest UNFCCC report found is NC3, published 25 Jul 2025.

YEM.notes: Yemen is a UNFCCC Non-Annex I/LDC country and, because it has signed but not ratified the Paris Agreement, its UNFCCC NDC registry entry is in the archive even though Yemen submitted an NDC 3.0 Vision in November 2025; the document says measurable mitigation and adaptation targets are to be finalized in 2026.
YEM.ndc_target: No quantified economy-wide GHG reduction target in active NDC 3.0 Vision; headline mitigation goal is at least 35% renewable energy share in total generation by 2035.
YEM.latest_un_report: BUR1, 2 Oct 2018; no BTR found as of 2026

NER.notes: Niger’s 2026 NDC 3.0 covers 2025–2035 and raises the mitigation goal, but official material found indicates a long-term low-carbon strategy targeting an 80% emissions reduction by 2050 rather than a formal net-zero target; no compliance carbon tax or ETS is listed as implemented for Niger in the World Bank carbon-pricing dashboard.
NER.ndc_target: -51.2% GHG by 2035 vs BAU, including -13% unconditional; interim -39.7% by 2030 vs BAU.
NER.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 21 Sep 2016.

SSD.notes: South Sudan’s active NDC is its second NDC submitted in September 2021; it is a conditional, sectoral mitigation-and-sequestration package rather than a percentage reduction against a base year, and South Sudan has no implemented carbon tax or ETS listed by the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard.
SSD.ndc_target: Conditional measures to reduce 109.87 MtCO2e and sequester an additional 45.06 MtCO2e by 2030, with international support.
SSD.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 23 Feb 2021, entered into force for South Sudan 25 Mar 2021.
SSD.latest_un_report: NC1, 19 Aug 2019; no BTR1 shown as submitted in the UNFCCC BTR1 table as of its 8 Sep 2026 update.

MLI.notes: Mali is an LDC/Non-Annex I Party and, as of the latest official UNFCCC submissions found, its current NDC remains the 2021 updated NDC while NDC 3.0 was reportedly under domestic validation in 2026 but not found as an official UNFCCC submission.
MLI.ndc_target: Reduce GHG emissions by 31% in energy, 25% in agriculture, 39% in land use/forestry, and 31% in waste by 2030 vs business-as-usual, equivalent to about a 40% total reduction vs BAU.
MLI.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 23 Sep 2016.
MLI.latest_un_report: NC4, Dec 2025; latest transparency-specific report: BUR1, 28 Aug 2023. No BTR1 listed as submitted on the UNFCCC BTR table last updated 8 Sep 2026.

CHE.notes: Switzerland’s 2050 net-zero target is enshrined in the Climate and Innovation Act, in force from 1 Jan 2025; the NDC says the 2035 target is to be achieved primarily through domestic measures, while Article 6 cooperation remains part of Swiss policy.
CHE.ndc_target: At least -65% GHG by 2035 vs 1990, implemented as a 2031–2035 emissions budget; current 2030 NDC remains at least -50% by 2030 vs 1990.

carbon_pricing.name: CO₂ levy on fossil thermal fuels
carbon_pricing.price: CHF 120/tCO₂ (in force as of 2026)

carbon_pricing.name: Swiss Emissions Trading System (installations; linked to EU ETS)
carbon_pricing.price: €74.32/tCO₂ clearing price at Sep. 2025 Swiss auction

carbon_pricing.name: Swiss ETS for aircraft operators
carbon_pricing.price: Same Swiss/EU-linked allowance market; recent official Swiss auction clearing price €74.32/tCO₂ (Sep. 2025)

DOM.notes: The Dominican Republic filed an active NDC 3.0 with the UNFCCC on 9 Jun 2026; its 2050 climate-neutrality/carbon-neutrality objective is being pursued through a long-term strategy process rather than an enacted net-zero law, and the World Bank lists a Dominican Republic ETS as under consideration, not implemented, with no price data.
DOM.ndc_target: -32% GHG by 2035 vs business-as-usual; interim -28% by 2030
DOM.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 21 Sep 2017

AFG.notes: Afghanistan’s active UNFCCC NDC registry entry remains its first NDC, originally communicated in 2016 and published in the registry file set in 2022; the country is an LDC and its target is entirely conditional on support.
AFG.ndc_target: Conditional 13.6% reduction in GHG emissions by 2030 compared with a 2030 business-as-usual scenario, subject to external support.
AFG.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 15 Feb 2017, in force for Afghanistan 17 Mar 2017.
AFG.latest_un_report: BUR1, 13 Oct 2019; associated NIR submitted 1 Mar 2020. No BTR1 listed by UNFCCC as of Sep 2026.

CIV.notes: No carbon tax or ETS is in force: the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard lists a Côte d’Ivoire carbon tax only as under consideration, while OECD states Côte d’Ivoire does not operate an ETS or levy a carbon tax; the 2030 carbon-neutrality reference comes from the 2022 NDC’s conditional AFOLU ambition, with no separate net-zero law found in official sources.
CIV.ndc_target: -33.07% GHG by 2035 vs BAU; up to -74.29% conditional on international support
CIV.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 25 Oct 2016, entered into force 24 Nov 2016
CIV.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 20 Dec 2024; related CTF/CRT tables submitted 28 Mar 2025

SVK.notes: Slovakia has no explicit national carbon tax; its explicit carbon pricing is mainly through the EU ETS, and the planned EU ETS2 for buildings and road transport is not yet in force as of 25 Oct 2026.
SVK.ndc_target: As part of the EU joint NDC: indicative -66.25% to -72.5% net GHG by 2035 vs 1990, while reiterating at least -55% net GHG by 2030 vs 1990.
SVK.paris_status: Party; Slovakia ratified the Paris Agreement on 5 Oct 2016 and it entered into force for Slovakia on 4 Nov 2016.

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)
carbon_pricing.price: €79.67/tCO2 average 2026 EUA reference price as of 25 Oct 2026

carbon_pricing.name: National carbon tax
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

TTO.notes: Trinidad and Tobago’s 2026 Second NDC is sectoral rather than economy-wide, and its headline 2035 mitigation target is contingent on international support; the updated National Climate Change Policy commits to prepare a Net-Zero Roadmap toward a net-zero GHG state before 2100, but no carbon tax or ETS is listed as implemented by the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard as of 2026.
TTO.ndc_target: Conditional 15% reduction in cumulative GHG emissions in power generation, transport and industry by 2035 vs BAU using 2013 base year; unconditional 30% cut in public transport emissions by 2030 vs BAU.
TTO.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 22 Feb 2018, in force for Trinidad and Tobago 24 Mar 2018.

LKA.notes: Sri Lanka’s latest NDC is NDC 3.0, submitted to the UNFCCC on 25 Sep 2025; the 2050 carbon-neutrality goal is in the NDC/Carbon Net Zero 2050 Roadmap approved by Cabinet, not a standalone climate law, and OECD’s 2024 country note says Sri Lanka has no explicit carbon price and no positive Net Effective Carbon Rate in 2023.
LKA.ndc_target: Reduce total GHG emissions by 20.09% below BAU over 2026–2035, comprising 8.11% unconditional and 11.98% conditional on international support; also increase net carbon removals by 4.49% below BAU.
LKA.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 21 Sep 2016.

carbon_pricing.name: Carbon tax
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

carbon_pricing.name: Emissions trading system
carbon_pricing.price: n/a

LKA.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 31 Dec 2024; publication date 03 Jan 2025.

LAO.notes: As of 25 Oct 2026, Laos’ NDC 3.0 appeared to be in finalization/endorsement rather than recorded as submitted to the UNFCCC, so the current official NDC headline remains the 2021 updated NDC; the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard lists no Lao carbon tax or ETS in force.
LAO.ndc_target: 60% GHG reduction by 2030 compared with baseline, about 62,000 ktCO2e in absolute terms; conditional pathway is framed toward net-zero GHG emissions by 2050.
LAO.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 7 Sep 2016, in force 4 Nov 2016.
LAO.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 24 Dec 2025; UNFCCC publication date 5 Jan 2026.

PNG.notes: No compliance carbon tax or ETS with a market price was found in force as of 2026; PNG has carbon-market regulations for carbon projects/Article 6-style mitigation outcomes, while an earlier liquid-fuels carbon levy was reportedly stopped after one year due to constitutional revenue-law issues.
PNG.ndc_target: NDC 3.0 (2025–2035): net-zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative by 2035; includes 29% energy-sector emissions reduction by 2035, 80% on-grid renewable electricity by 2035, and LULUCF removals of about -17,000 Gg CO2e by 2030 and -18,000 Gg CO2e by 2035.
PNG.paris_status: Party; Papua New Guinea ratified the Paris Agreement on 21 September 2016 and it entered into force for PNG on 4 November 2016.
PNG.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 05 Jan 2026 (2024 Biennial Transparency Report); CTF/CRT annex files published Sep 2026.

MDG.notes: Madagascar’s 2026 NDC 3.0 frames the country as already a large net carbon sink (-108.8 MtCO2e in 2023) and focuses on preserving that sink plus sectoral mitigation and adaptation, rather than setting a legally binding net-zero year; the World Bank carbon-pricing dashboard lists no Madagascar ETS or carbon tax in force.
MDG.ndc_target: Reduce non-AFAT emissions 34.0% below the reference scenario by 2035, avoiding 14.6 MtCO2e, while maintaining a net-negative national GHG balance.
MDG.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 21 Sep 2016.
MDG.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 20 Mar 2026; 2024 CRT submitted 29 Apr 2026.

JOR.notes: Jordan’s 2022–2050 climate policy frames 2050 as carbon neutrality/part of the global effort toward carbon neutrality, not as a net-zero target enacted in law; no carbon tax or ETS is listed as implemented for Jordan in the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard as of 2026.
JOR.ndc_target: -5% unconditional and up to -31% conditional GHG emissions by 2035 vs business-as-usual, under Jordan’s NDC 3.0.
JOR.paris_status: Party; ratified 4 Nov 2016, entry into force for Jordan 4 Dec 2016.

SOM.notes: Somalia is an LDC with a very small global emissions share; its current NDC is adaptation-heavy and relies significantly on international finance, while its 2025 LT-LEDS launch signals a low-emission pathway but not a clear net-zero year.
SOM.ndc_target: Reduce GHG emissions by 34% by 2035 relative to business-as-usual, under NDC 3.0.
SOM.paris_status: Party; Somalia ratified the Paris Agreement on 22 April 2016.
SOM.latest_un_report: BUR1, 3 Apr 2023; no BTR1 listed for Somalia on the UNFCCC First BTR table as of its 8 Sep 2026 update.

SEN.notes: Senegal has a carbon tax only under consideration, not in force, so there is no implemented carbon tax or ETS price to report.
SEN.ndc_target: -7% unconditional and -29.5% conditional GHG emissions by 2030 vs business-as-usual baseline projections.
SEN.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 21 Sep 2016.
SEN.latest_un_report: BUR1, submitted 19 Jan 2025; no BTR listed in UNFCCC reports as of Oct 2026.

GTM.notes: Guatemala’s 2050 net-zero carbon goal is in its LT-LEDS rather than in a climate law, and OECD/World Bank-style carbon-pricing sources show no explicit carbon tax or ETS in force as of 2026.
GTM.ndc_target: Unconditional 11.2% GHG reduction by 2030 versus BAU; conditional up to 22.6% with international support.
GTM.latest_un_report: BTR1, submitted 24 Mar 2025; CRT submitted 25 Mar 2025

LTU.notes: Lithuania is covered by the EU’s joint NDC, while its national climate agenda sets a domestic 2030 goal of -30% GHG vs 2005 including LULUCF and a 2050 circular, climate-neutral economy goal.
LTU.ndc_target: EU joint NDC: at least -55% net GHG emissions by 2030 vs 1990
LTU.paris_status: Party; Paris Agreement ratified by Lithuania under Law No. XIII-184 and in force for Lithuania since 4 Mar 2017

carbon_pricing.name: EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)
carbon_pricing.price: about €73/tCO2e (US$85), 2026 World Bank dashboard

carbon_pricing.name: Lithuania CO2 component in excise duties on energy products
carbon_pricing.price: 2026 statutory rates vary by fuel: e.g. gasoline €96/1,000 l; standard diesel €53.6/1,000 l; coal €87.2/t; coke/lignite €128/t

GIN.notes: Guinea updated its NDC in November 2025 to a 2035 target; official UNFCCC reporting pages show a BUR1 but no Biennial Transparency Report entry, and the World Bank carbon-pricing sources do not list a Guinea carbon tax or ETS in force.
GIN.ndc_target: -17% unconditional and -49% conditional GHG emissions by 2035 vs BAU, economy-wide including AFOLU
GIN.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016 and ratified 21 Sep 2016
GIN.latest_un_report: BUR1, 8 Sep 2024; no BTR listed for Guinea on the UNFCCC BTR table as of 2026, and NC3 was submitted 7 Nov 2025

ZWE.notes: Zimbabwe’s 2025 NDC3.0 replaced the 2030 NDC headline with a 2035 per-capita BAU target; it has Article 6/carbon-credit regulations and a carbon-markets authority, but no domestic cap-and-trade ETS was found in force.
ZWE.ndc_target: At least 40% reduction in GHG emissions per capita by 2035 vs 2035 BAU, with 27 mitigation measures estimated to reduce emissions by 50,104 Gg CO2e.
ZWE.paris_status: Party; signed 22 Apr 2016, ratified 7 Aug 2017, in force for Zimbabwe 6 Sep 2017.

carbon_pricing.name: Carbon tax on petroleum fuels
carbon_pricing.price: US$0.013/L diesel and US$0.040/L petrol, or 2%/6% of CIF respectively, in consolidated Finance Act text updated to Dec 2024; current 2026 pump-price build-ups also show a carbon-tax line of about US$0.030/L.

ZWE.latest_un_report: BTR1/NC5 submitted 31 Dec 2024; BTR1 Article 6 annex submitted 22 Aug 2025; 2024 NID submitted 2 Feb 2026.

PRI.notes: Puerto Rico’s binding climate policy is domestic/subnational: Act 33-2019 and energy laws require climate planning and a 100% renewable-electricity pathway by 2050, but this is not an economy-wide NDC or net-zero target; Puerto Rico’s 2024 Priority Climate Action Plan lists carbon pricing only as a possible measure, not an instrument in force.
PRI.ndc_target: none; Puerto Rico has no separate NDC, and the United States is not currently a Party to the Paris Agreement as of 27 Jan 2026
PRI.paris_status: Not a Party in its own right; U.S. Paris Agreement withdrawal took effect 27 Jan 2026
PRI.latest_un_report: none; Puerto Rico submits no separate UNFCCC transparency reports (latest U.S. BTR was submitted in Dec 2024, before U.S. Paris withdrawal took effect)

BIH.notes: Bosnia and Herzegovina has a 2050 climate-neutrality pledge through the Sofia Declaration/Green Agenda for the Western Balkans, but official reporting and EU assessments indicate no enacted state-level climate law or adopted 2050 net-zero/climate-neutrality objective; as of 2026, domestic carbon pricing is still under discussion and no carbon tax or ETS is in force.
BIH.ndc_target: Unconditional -33.2% GHG by 2030 vs 1990; conditional -36.8% with international support.

MOZ.notes: Mozambique is an LDC and frames its NDC as highly conditional on international finance; its 2025 provisional NDC says the long-term low-emissions strategy is still under development and sets a 2050 emissions trajectory, not a legally binding net-zero target.
MOZ.ndc_target: Provisional NDC 3.0: conditional reduction of GHG emissions by 15–25% below the 2020 BUR2 baseline/BAU by 2035; final quantified target still under development.
MOZ.paris_status: Party; ratified 4 June 2018, entry into force 4 July 2018.
MOZ.latest_un_report: BUR2, submitted 11 Dec 2024; Mozambique had no BTR1/BTR2 listed in UNFCCC BTR tables as of the 2026 UNFCCC pages checked.
